```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
library(splines)
library(caret)
library(mice)
```

```{r load-data}
data("diamonds", package = "ggplot2")
data("sim5",    package = "modelr")
```

## Task 1: Natural spline fits on sim5

```{r task1}
mods_spline <- list(
  df1 = lm(y ~ ns(x, 1), data = sim5),
  df3 = lm(y ~ ns(x, 3), data = sim5),
  df5 = lm(y ~ ns(x, 5), data = sim5)
)

grid5 <- sim5 |>
  data_grid(x = seq_range(x, n = 100)) |>
  gather_predictions(!!!mods_spline)

ggplot(sim5, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(data = grid5, aes(y = pred, colour = model), linewidth = 1) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1",
                      labels = c("df = 1", "df = 3", "df = 5")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Natural spline fits on sim5 (sinusoidal data)",
    subtitle = "df = 1 underfits; df = 5 captures the full sine pattern.",
    colour   = "Spline df"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Task 2: 10-fold CV to choose df

```{r task2}
set.seed(42)
cv_results <- tibble(
  df      = 1:8,
  cv_rmse = sapply(1:8, function(df) {
    folds <- createFolds(sim5$y, k = 10)
    mean(sapply(folds, function(idx) {
      train <- sim5[-idx, ]
      test  <- sim5[ idx, ]
      pred  <- predict(lm(y ~ ns(x, df), data = train), newdata = test)
      sqrt(mean((test$y - pred)^2))
    }))
  })
)

best_df <- cv_results$df[which.min(cv_results$cv_rmse)]
cat("Optimal df:", best_df, "(CV-RMSE =", round(min(cv_results$cv_rmse), 3), ")\n")

ggplot(cv_results, aes(df, cv_rmse)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(colour = "darkorange", size = 3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = best_df, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  labs(
    title    = "10-fold CV RMSE vs spline degrees of freedom (sim5)",
    subtitle = paste0("Optimal df = ", best_df, " (red dashed line)."),
    x        = "Degrees of freedom",
    y        = "CV RMSE"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Task 3: na.omit vs na.exclude

```{r task3}
set.seed(99)
diam_miss <- diamonds |>
  mutate(carat = ifelse(runif(n()) < 0.10, NA, carat))

# Default: na.omit (rows with NA are dropped entirely)
mod_omit <- lm(log(price) ~ log(carat), data = diam_miss)
cat("na.omit:   nobs =", nobs(mod_omit), "\n")
cat("na.omit:   length(residuals) =", length(residuals(mod_omit)), "\n")

# na.exclude: rows with NA dropped but positions preserved in output
mod_excl <- lm(log(price) ~ log(carat), data = diam_miss,
               na.action = na.exclude)
cat("na.exclude: nobs =", nobs(mod_excl), "\n")
cat("na.exclude: length(residuals) =", length(residuals(mod_excl)), "\n")

# With na.exclude, length(residuals) = nrow(diam_miss) = 53,940.
# The NA positions are preserved as NA in the residuals vector,
# making it easy to cbind() back to the original data frame.
# With na.omit, length(residuals) = nobs (only complete cases).
```

## Task 4: Multiple imputation with mice

```{r task4}
set.seed(1)
diam_miss2 <- diamonds |>
  mutate(carat = ifelse(runif(n()) < 0.10, NA, carat))

# Multiple imputation: 5 complete datasets
imp <- mice(
  diam_miss2 |> select(price, carat, cut),
  m         = 5,
  method    = "pmm",
  printFlag = FALSE
)

# Fit model on each imputed dataset and pool estimates
fit_mi <- with(imp, lm(log(price) ~ log(carat) + cut))
pool_summary <- pool(fit_mi) |> summary()
print(pool_summary)

# Compare to complete-case analysis
mod_cc <- lm(log(price) ~ log(carat) + cut,
             data = diam_miss2 |> filter(!is.na(carat)))
cat("\nComplete-case log(carat) std.error:",
    round(summary(mod_cc)$coefficients["log(carat)", "Std. Error"], 5), "\n")
cat("MI pooled  log(carat) std.error:  ",
    round(pool_summary[pool_summary$term == "log(carat)", "std.error"], 5), "\n")

# MI standard errors are slightly larger than complete-case because
# MI propagates the additional uncertainty due to the missing values
# (between-imputation variance) via Rubin's rules.
```
